intro.title: Quality Assurance That Protects Every Release
paragraphs: Bugs that reach production cost far more than bugs caught early: lost customers, support tickets, emergency fixes and damage to your reputation. Software quality assurance builds checks into the whole development process, so problems are found and fixed long before users see them.

Our QA testing services cover the full range of software testing. Manual testers explore your product like real users. Automation engineers build test suites that run on every change, so regression testing takes minutes instead of days. Specialists test APIs, databases, performance under load, security vulnerabilities, accessibility, compatibility and localisation. Everything is documented in clear test plans, test cases and reports.

You can hire us for a single testing project, set up test automation for your team, or outsource QA completely as QA as a service. We test web apps, mobile apps, SaaS products, ecommerce stores, ERP and CRM systems and more. Building software with us? Testing is included in every <sd>software development</sd> project. Otherwise, <contact>tell us what you need tested</contact>.

faqs.title: QA & Software Testing FAQs
faqs.subtitle: Quick answers about software testing and quality assurance.

items.q: What is the difference between QA and software testing?
items.a: Quality assurance is the overall process of preventing defects, including standards, reviews and test strategy. Software testing is the part of QA that checks the software to find defects. We provide both.

items.q: Should we use manual testing or automation testing?
items.a: Both. Manual testing is best for exploratory, usability and new features. Automation testing is best for repetitive checks like regression, API and smoke tests that run on every release. Most products need a mix.

items.q: What is the difference between functional and non-functional testing?
items.a: Functional testing checks what the software does, such as features and business rules. Non-functional testing checks how well it does it, such as performance, security, usability, accessibility and compatibility.

items.q: What is regression testing and why automate it?
items.a: Regression testing makes sure new changes have not broken existing features. Because it must be repeated for every release, automating it saves time, reduces human error and lets teams release faster.

items.q: Do you provide security and penetration testing?
items.a: Yes. We run vulnerability scanning and penetration testing based on OWASP guidelines for web apps, mobile apps and APIs, and provide a report with risks and recommended fixes.

items.q: How do you fit testing into agile and CI/CD?
items.a: We verify work within each sprint, write test cases alongside development and run automated tests in your CI/CD pipeline on every change, so defects are found early. This is often called shift-left testing.

items.q: How much does QA outsourcing cost?
items.a: A one-off testing project typically costs $1,500 to $5,000, test automation setup $5,000 to $20,000, and ongoing QA as a service starts from around $1,500 per month, depending on scope.
